constraints.evidence: Slide 8 sizes the target at $41.9M on ~$1,398M of sales. The bridge reaches $40.7M (2.9%), with a 3.1% stretch. The shortfall against 3.0% is shown, not hidden.

Slides 15 and 17 compare a ~$26M Wave 1 run-rate, with phasing at 60% and one-third, against the $20M covenant. That is a run-rate, not FY2026 income. Slide 20 says FY2026 is closing now, FY2025 is used as the run-rate, and the covenant may already be fixed. FY2026 operating income is never estimated, and the downside case is not tested against $20M.
Slide 16 itemises $20.1M against the $25M cap, leaving $4.9M of headroom. The $7.5M lease exit is flagged as the only figure from the pack, and Wave 1 spend is shown as $5.4M.
Slide 12 and decision 5 separate the six leases expiring by 2027 (management decision) from the three that need a board vote, which is set for Q2 FY2027. Scenario C shows the plan without the three.
Delivery is kept as 'repriced home delivery plus free click-and-collect'. Option D (exit delivery) is shown as breaking the owners' commitment, and decision 6 confirms the position with the owners.
A $7.3M wage step is deducted in the bridge (−3.6 base, half recovered; −7.3 low case). The recovery assumption is unsupported.

Slide 7 gives −$10.4M after third-party delivery and 30% incrementality, and rebuts the team's 6.1% claim. It shows −$12.34 per delivered order and the rise in home-delivery share. The 3% proposal ($0.3M) is named but not folded into the base numbers. The frozen service still loses $7.6M.
Slide 11 nets the $14.5M cut: shrink response up to −$10.0M (0.67 pt) and −$3.0M per 1% of sales lost. That gives +1.5 to +14.5, central ~+4.5. It uses $1.5M per 0.1 pt and the quartile gradient.

Promotions +5.1 is net of a 1% sales loss ($2.8M). ValuMart comps of −4.2% and the price-perception shift (33% to 41%) are cited, with a $2M everyday-price reinvestment as mitigation. However, the base case also assumes vendor funding recovers from 46% to 50% (+$3.6M), which the checklist says should not be assumed.

The headline is the $6.6M net figure, built from 25% transfer at 12% contribution. Timing (six exits by end-2027) and the $7.5M exit cost are stated, and store exits are excluded from the Wave 1 covenant run-rate.

alternatives.evidence: Slide 11 and option A compare the 8% blanket cut ($13–26M, 0.9–1.7%) with a targeted rebalance (+$3.6M). The targeted version is confined to Q3–Q4 stores, protects produce and receiving hours, and carries a reverse-if-shrink-rises-0.2pt rule, with shrink tracked at Gate 1.

Slide 10 sizes the fee rollout at +$2.5–2.8M and the contract re-tender at $0.5M per 5%. Exiting delivery (option D) is sized at ~$6.4M more and rejected as breaking the owners' commitment. Both are shown side by side.

The plan adopts pruning the loss-making events, supported by the 38% post-event review, and rebuts the category team's comp claim on slide 6. The target is 25% rather than 24%, with the volume loss netted off. The saving is not split out by the share that comes from the losing events.

Slide 12 compares the six at expiry (+$4.4M, no exit cost, ~0.5 year payback) with all nine (+$6.6M) and the three alone (+$2.2M, 3.9 year payback). Option C is the plan without the three. 'Close none' is implicit.

sensitivities.evidence: Shrink at $1.5M per 0.1 pt. A 0.67 pt response gives −$10.0M, and each 1% of sales lost costs $3.0M. Net range +1.5 to +14.5, and A falls to $13.2M. The covenant-breaking shrink rise (~+0.65 pt) and the full-wipe-out point (~+1 pt) are not stated explicitly.

Click-and-collect breaks even at 38.5% incrementality (the document assumes 30%). The delivery-pricing range is 2.2–3.3, with a pause trigger at a 5% sales fall. The caveat on the 4-store test is stated. The total e-commerce loss is not recomputed across cannibalisation rates, and the document does not show that the loss-making conclusion holds up to ~29% incrementality.

Slide 17 gives ±$2.0M per 1 pt of promotion share and −$2.8M per 1% of sales lost. The promotions low case is 3.5 against a base of 5.1. The document does not state the loss of sales that erases the saving (~1.8% more). It also does not size the share of the saving that comes from the 38% of events that lose money.

overclaim.quote: Taking shrink back to FY2023's 2.1% closes the gap to the 3.0% target (3.1%).

omissions: There is no estimate of FY2026 operating income, which is the year the lender covenant tests. The plan substitutes a six-month run-rate. The slide 17 title says even the FY2028 low case is 'well above the $20M level the lender requires', which compares a FY2028 figure to a FY2026 test.

The base case is 2.9%, below the 3.0% target. The 3.1% stretch relies on the shrink-to-2.1% lever, which slide 18 also counts as contingency for covering a vendor-funding or wage-step miss. The contingency and the stretch cannot both be spent, and the document does not say so.

The plan holds FY2025 prices and has no baseline erosion. ValuMart has opened 11 stores and comps are −4.2% near them, but no drift in sales or margin is modelled, even though the base case is only 0.1 pt from the target.
The provider's proposed 3% delivery rate rise ($0.3M) is named but is not netted from the +$2.5M delivery-pricing figure.
unsupported_assumptions: "Cutting 4 pt of promotion share loses 1% of total sales at 20¢" is the only basis for netting the promotions lever. It is not from the pack, and it is far smaller than the −4.2% comps seen near ValuMart.

"Vendor funding (46%→50%)" is worth +$3.6M. It rests on reading the 14-pt gap as net of funding, which the document admits the pack does not say. The document itself calls this the least certain number.

"2027 wage step ... half recovered in prices" turns −$7.3M into −$3.6M. There is no evidence of pricing power, and the plan is cutting promotions while 41% of customers already call Harlow more expensive.
"Private label 18.5%→20.5%" (+$3.4M) is justified only by extending the FY2023–25 trend of +0.75 pt a year. The $2.0M cost is a planning allowance.
"Labor rebalance +3.6" assumes shrink stays "neutral to positive" because Q3 and Q4 differ by 0.1 pt. The per-quartile hours split is not in the pack, and the quartile view is a correlation.
"Shrink 2.6%→2.3%" (+$4.2M) is credited to a $4.0M programme that is a planning assumption, on the basis that Q3–Q4 stores are already at 2.3–2.4%.

"Totals split pro rata by store count" gives the +$4.4M for six stores and +$2.2M for three. The split that drives the covenant-timing and board-vote decision is not in the pack, and the $0.4M per store closure cost is also assumed.
Only $7.5M of the $20.1M one-time cost comes from the pack. The other $12.6M is assumption, so the $4.9M headroom is uncertain.
"Wave 1 run-rate ~$26M" uses 60% of promotions and one-third of shrink phasing. No basis is given for the phasing, and the figure is a run-rate rather than FY2026 income.
